_meta.title: EN→FR lexicon for the Velocity White Papers
_meta.purpose: Binding term map + typography rules, derived from the Government of Alberta francophone reviewers' corrections (2026-06-12). Loaded into the translation model prompt. Human-readable guide: docs/fr-style-guide.md.

typography.apostrophe: Use the curly apostrophe ’ (U+2019), never the straight '.
typography.quotes: Use guillemets « … » with non-breaking spaces inside.
typography.em_dash: The spaced em dash — like this — is allowed in French (this overrides the English no-em-dash rule). 'non pas X, mais Y' / 'non seulement X, mais Y' are fine.
typography.percent: Numerals with a space before %, e.g. 95 %.
typography.thousands: Space as the thousands separator: 5 500, 189 millions.
typography.money: Spell the unit in prose: 'millions de dollars', 'milliards de dollars'. Never M$ or G$.
typography.ranges: Non-breaking hyphen ‑ in ranges and compounds: 2024‑2025, main‑d’œuvre.
typography.numbers: Use numerals for quantities of two or more digits and for round large figures (70 par année, 40 ans, 2 milliards).

tone: Canadian public-administration French; calm, clear, institutional voice (nous / l’Alberta).
Plain language: prefer the everyday word; split long English sentences.
Soften incidental siege/war metaphors to plain nouns; keep a metaphor only when it is the paper’s central image.
Do not name AI vendors gratuitously; generalize to 'les modèles actuels' unless the name is substantive and cited.
Inclusive phrasing where natural: celles et ceux, toutes et tous.

labels.numbered_reference: Livre blanc N (or Document N) — never 'papier'.
